problems.title: Triangle formed by parabola intercepts
problems.question: The graph y=-x²+4x+a meets the axes at A,B,C, with A=(-1,0). Find the area of ABC.
problems.idea: Use the known root to find a, then the other intercepts.
formulas: Triangle area=base·height/2; a point on a graph satisfies its equation.
steps: At x=-1,y=0, the equation is -1-4+a=0, giving a=5.
The x-intercepts solve -x²+4x+5=0, giving x=-1,5. Hence AB=6.
The y-intercept is C=(0,5), giving height 5.

problems.title: A quadratic range includes its minimum
problems.question: Find a if y=x²+2x+a-2 has range (-1,∞).
problems.idea: A real upward-opening quadratic attains its minimum.
steps: The minimum is a-3, attained at x=-1.
Therefore the range is always [a-3,∞), with a closed left endpoint.
It cannot equal the open interval (-1,∞) for any a.
problems.note: If the intended range were [-1,∞), then a=2. The printed open endpoint changes the answer.

problems.title: A cube-sum quotient from Vieta’s formulas
problems.question: If x₁,x₂ solve $2x^2-5x+2=0$, find $(x_1^3+x_2^3)/(x_1+x_2)$.
problems.idea: Factor the sum of cubes and express the result through root sum and product.
steps: The root sum is 5/2 and product is 1.
The sum is nonzero, so the quotient equals (5/2)²-3·1.

problems.title: An odd-value condition fixes the constant
problems.question: For f(x)=x²+bx+c, suppose f(1)=-f(-1). Which listed comparison must hold?
problems.idea: Add the two values to eliminate b.
steps: For every real b, b²≥0>-4=4c, hence b²>4c.

problems.title: The vertex lies outside the allowed interval
problems.question: Find the minimum of y=197(198-x)²-199 on [199,2015].
problems.idea: Choose the allowed x nearest the vertex x=198.
formulas: The square (x-198)² increases as x moves right of 198.
steps: Every allowed x is at least 199, so the closest is x=199.

problems.title: Scaling the input scales the roots
problems.question: The roots of ax²+bx+c=0 are 2,3. Find the smaller root of 4ax²+2bx+c=0.
problems.idea: The new polynomial is the original evaluated at 2x.
formulas: If P(t)=0 at t=2,3, then P(2x)=0 requires 2x=2 or 3.
steps: The new roots are x=1 and x=3/2.

problems.title: A square less than one
problems.question: Solve (x-2)²<1.
problems.idea: Convert the square bound to an absolute-value bound.

problems.title: Transform the y-intercept
problems.question: The graph y=f(x) meets the y-axis at (0,-4). Where does y=|f(x)|+3 meet it?
problems.idea: At the y-axis the input remains x=0.
formulas: A y-intercept is found by setting x=0.

problems.title: A squared denominator controls the sign
problems.question: Solve $(x^2-1)/(2x-1)^2>0$.
problems.idea: The denominator is positive wherever it is defined.
formulas: A nonzero square is positive; x²-1=(x-1)(x+1).
steps: The quotient is positive exactly where x²-1>0, which gives x<-1 or x>1.
Those intervals already avoid x=1/2, and the roots ±1 are excluded by the strict inequality.

problems.title: Exactly three roots of an absolute quadratic
problems.question: For which a does |x²-2x-3|=a have exactly three distinct real roots?
problems.idea: Write the quadratic as (x-1)²-4 and count intersections with the levels ±a.
steps: The first equation gives two roots whenever a≥0.
For 0<a<4, the second also has two different roots; for a>4 it has none.
At a=4, the second equation gives the single root x=1, in addition to the two roots of the first.
At a=0 the two equations coincide and give only two distinct roots.

problems.title: A tangency gives a double root
problems.question: The graph y=-ax²+bx+2 touches the x-axis at (1,0). Find a+b.
problems.idea: A tangent quadratic at that point is a multiple of (x-1)².
formulas: A double root at 1 gives y=k(x-1)².

problems.title: Check both radical-equation roots
problems.question: Find the product of the roots of $\sqrt{2x^2+6}=x+2$.
problems.idea: Require x≥-2, then square.
formulas: Squaring requires checking the original nonnegative right side.
steps: The roots are 2±√2; both exceed -2 and satisfy the original equation.
Their product is the constant term 2 of the monic quadratic.

problems.title: Axis-intercept triangle of an absolute quadratic
problems.question: Find the area of the triangle formed by the axis intercepts of y=-|x²-2x-1|+7.
problems.idea: Find the horizontal intercepts and the vertical height.
steps: At y=0, |x²-2x-1|=7. The positive case gives x²-2x-8=0, with roots -2 and 4.
The negative case would give x²-2x+6=0, which has no real roots.
The base length is 6 and the height is 6, so the area is 18.

problems.title: A perfect-square discriminant
problems.question: For which b does x²-x+b-b²=0 have exactly one distinct real root?
problems.idea: The leading coefficient is always nonzero, so set the discriminant to zero.

problems.title: A decreasing quadratic on a short interval
problems.question: Find the minimum of y=3x²-24x-25 on [0,3].
problems.idea: Locate the vertex before checking the interval endpoints.
steps: The vertex is at x=4, outside the interval to its right.
On [0,3], the distance to 4 decreases as x increases, so the function decreases.

problems.title: Rectangle area from its perimeter and diagonal
problems.question: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm and diagonal 8 cm. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the square of the side sum.

problems.title: Area of a tangential right trapezoid
problems.question: A right trapezoid has two angles differing by 120° and inradius 3 cm. Find its area.
problems.idea: The nonright angles are 30° and 150°.
formulas: Height=2r; slanted leg=h/sin30°; base sum=leg sum for a tangential quadrilateral.
steps: The height and perpendicular leg are 6.

problems.title: Two medians form a 6-8-10 right triangle at the centroid
problems.question: Two medians of a triangle are 9 and 12, and the side joining their originating vertices is 10. Find the area.
problems.idea: The centroid shortens both medians to two thirds.
formulas: Vertex-to-centroid distance=2/3 of the median; the centroid forms three equal-area triangles with the sides.
steps: The two centroid segments have lengths 6 and 8.
Their endpoints are 10 apart, and 6²+8²=10², so they are perpendicular.
Their triangle with the centroid has area 6·8/2=24.
This is one third of the original area, giving 3·24=72.

problems.title: Which altitude piece is the inradius?
problems.question: An isosceles triangle’s incenter divides its altitude to the base into lengths 5 and 3 cm. Find the area.
problems.idea: The inradius is the smaller piece next to the base.
formulas: r=area/semiperimeter; for an isosceles triangle r<h/2.
steps: The altitude is h=8. Since r<4, the base-to-incenter piece must be r=3.
Let half the base be u and the equal side be ℓ=√(u²+64). Then 3=8u/(u+ℓ).
This gives ℓ=5u/3. Squaring yields 25u²/9=u²+64, hence u=6.
The base is 12, and the area is 12·8/2=48.

problems.title: Area ratio of two triangles linked by altitudes
problems.question: ABC has area 25 cm². Altitudes AA₁ and BB₁ meet sides BC and AC. Given AC=15 and A₁C=6, find the area of A₁CB₁.
problems.idea: The smaller triangle has the same included angle C, and its two adjacent sides are projections.
steps: Each adjacent side of the smaller triangle is multiplied by |cosC| relative to the corresponding large-triangle side.
The area ratio is therefore cos²C=4/25.

problems.title: Heron’s formula for three unequal sides
problems.question: A triangle has sides 3,5,6 dm. Find its area.
problems.idea: Compute the semiperimeter first.

problems.title: Four parallel sections in a trapezoid
problems.question: Four lines parallel to bases 1 and 6 divide each trapezoid leg into five equal parts. Find the sum of the four interior section lengths.
problems.idea: Their lengths form an arithmetic progression.
steps: The sections at fifths of the height have lengths 2,3,4,5.

problems.title: Two parallel cuts of an angle
problems.question: Parallel BC and DE cut the sides of angle A, with B,D on one side. AB+AD=21 m, AC=12 m and AE=16 m. Find AB.
problems.idea: The two triangles with vertex A are similar.

problems.title: Rectangle side ratio from diagonal projections
problems.question: A perpendicular from a rectangle vertex to a diagonal divides it in ratio 1:3. The centre is 2 m from the longer side. Find its area.
problems.idea: The projection ratio is the ratio of squared legs in a right triangle.
formulas: For right-triangle legs, a²:b²=corresponding hypotenuse projections; centre-to-side distance=half the perpendicular side length.
steps: The squared side ratio is 1:3, so the longer side is 4√3.

problems.title: Area left near a square side
problems.question: Inside square ABCD of side 6 cm, BCE is equilateral. Find the area of triangle AED.
problems.idea: Use AD as the base and subtract the equilateral altitude from the square width.
steps: The equilateral altitude from E to BC is 6√3/2=3√3.
The distance from E to opposite side AD is 6-3√3.
